\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Query string on a buffer tape]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_bufferTape}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.queryString_bufferTape}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.queryString_eq_of_cells, Turing.OracleTM.queryTapeIdx}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c$ be a configuration of an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes, and let
$w$ be a finite word. If the content of the query tape of $c$ is the buffer tape storing
$w$, then the query string of $c$ is $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Step in the Query State]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_of_qQuery}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step_of_qQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle language, and let $c$ be a
configuration whose state is the query state of $M$. One step relative to $O$ leaves
every component of $c$ unchanged except its state, which becomes the positive-answer
state if the query string of $c$ belongs to $O$, and the negative-answer state
otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Oracle answer action]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.answerAction}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.answerAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
For a symbol $b$, the answer action for a machine with $k+1$ work tapes leaves the input
head and every work-tape head stationary, makes no work-tape writes, emits $b$, and
halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Step Under a Fixed Answer Action]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.step_of_answerAction}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.step_of_answerAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.answerAction, Turing.OracleTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine, let $O$ be an oracle language, and let $c$ be a
configuration whose state is $q$, where $q$ is not the query state of $M$. Suppose that
for every scanned input symbol and every tuple of scanned work-tape symbols, the
transition of $M$ in state $q$ is the action that emits the symbol $b$ and has no
successor state. Then one step from $c$ relative to $O$ leaves the state empty and
appends $b$ to the output, leaving all other configuration components unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Two-step behavior after an oracle query]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_two_of_qQuery}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_two_of_qQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.WellFormed, Turing.OracleTM.answerAction, Turing.OracleTM.queryString, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.OracleTM.step, Turing.OracleTM.step_of_answerAction, Turing.OracleTM.step_of_qQuery}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be an oracle machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes whose query state and two
answer states are pairwise distinct. Suppose that in the positive-answer state its
transition emits a fixed symbol $y$ and halts, for every scanned input symbol and tuple
of scanned work-tape symbols; suppose likewise that in the negative-answer state it
emits a fixed symbol $z$ and halts. Let $O$ be a language over the symbol alphabet, and
let $c$ be a configuration whose state is the query state. After two steps relative to
$O$, the machine is halted, and its output is the original output followed by $y$ if the
query string belongs to $O$, and by $z$ otherwise; all other components of the
configuration are unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Captured computation reaches the query state]
\lean{Turing.OracleTM.capture_reaches_qQuery}
\label{Turing.OracleTM.capture_reaches_qQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.exists_first_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM, Turing.OracleTM.plainEmptyOracle, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom, Turing.OracleTM.runFrom_eq_plainEmptyOracle, Turing.captureAction, Turing.captureCfg, Turing.capture_run}
\difficulty{5}
Let $S$ and $H$ be state sets, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $T$ be a natural
number. Let $tm$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes and state set
$S$, and let $M$ be an oracle Turing machine with $k$ ordinary work tapes and state set
$H$. Suppose there is a state map $e:S\to H$ whose image avoids the query state of $M$,
and suppose that on every state in the image of $e$, $M$'s transition agrees with the
capture transform of $tm$'s transition. For any oracle language $O$, Boolean words
$pre,out_0$, and initial configuration $c_0$ of $tm$, if $tm$ is halted after $T$ steps
from $c_0$, then there is a time $u\le T$ at which running $M$ with oracle $O$ from the
capture image of $c_0$ reaches the capture image of $tm$'s configuration after $T$
steps.
\end{theorem}
